title: Nigerian dishes that taste the same every time

say: Nigerian dishes that taste the same every time.
This is the video for Module 2 of Advanced Cooking and Nutrition: Nigerian and West African cuisine at a professional standard.
Ask ten cooks how they make stew and you get ten answers. In a business, that means Tuesday's stew is sweeter than Monday's.

say: Professional kitchens use a standard recipe: the same ingredients, the same weights, the same method, every time. A kitchen scale is the most important tool.

say: Fresh tomatoes are roughly 94% water. Step one. Blend your tomatoes, tatashe, which is red bell pepper, scotch bonnet and onion.

panel.heading: Stew base: reduce before you fry

say: Step two. Boil the blend uncovered until much of the water has gone. The common mistake is pouring it straight into hot oil. The oil spits and the stew can taste sour and raw.

say: Keep frying until the oil separates and rises to the top. That sign means the water has cooked out.

say: Then add stock and protein, taste, and adjust in small steps. Season lightly at the start, because flavour concentrates as it reduces.

say: Parboiled rice usually needs about 1.5 to 2 cups of water per cup of rice. Brands differ, so test once and write down what works for your rice and your pot.

say: NAFDAC has warned against using pesticides such as dichlorvos to preserve food. Buy beans from sellers you trust, reject any with a chemical smell or powdery residue, and wash and soak them well.

cards.d: Buy from trusted sellers. Reject beans with a chemical smell or powdery residue. Wash and soak well.

say: Bleaching palm oil gives heavy smoke and breaks down the oil. If you do it, use a small quantity, moderate heat, stay with the pot, open doors and windows, and never let it catch fire.

say: Think of the plate as a clock face. Protein at the front, starch at the back left and vegetables at the back right. Same layout every time.

panel.heading: Plates that look cared for

Add height with a rice mould
Clean rims; sauce next to, not across
Test and label every ladle and scoop

say: To remember. Weigh everything and write it on a recipe card. Boil down the blend and fry until the oil rises. Add leafy vegetables last so they stay green.
Test your yields and water ratios. And plate with a fixed layout, clean rims and garnish that belongs to the dish.
